result.title: End-to-End Stability of Online Active Learning in Large-Scale Neural Systems
result.summary: Online Active Learning (OAL) aims to extend deep learning from static inference after offline training to continuous adaptation during real-time interaction with a changing physical environment. This transition is essential for safety-critical applications, but it raises a central theoretical question: whether the online parameter update process remains stable when scaled to multilayer neural architectures. This paper develops a stability-focused OAL framework. The framework uses prediction error as a feedback signal to update a structured deep model, thereby linking online learning with Lyapunov-based energy minimization. We show that prediction error convergence alone is insufficient for global parameter convergence because multilayer networks may admit high-dimensional manifolds of equivalent output solutions. The analysis therefore separates output error regulation, internal zero dynamics, interlayer coupling, and parameter convergence. Persistency of excitation and active damping are then used to remove the residual null-space modes that remain after output error convergence. A cascaded Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic stability of the overall OAL learning process, while monotonic activation functions and diffeomorphic layer mappings provide the uniqueness condition for the target parameter trajectory. The resulting proof provides a theoretical basis for applying online adaptive learning to large-scale neural systems in nonstationary and safety-critical settings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出以稳定性为核心的在线主动学习框架：用预测误差作为反馈信号更新结构化深层模型参数，将在线学习与 Lyapunov 能量最小化联系起来，分层分析输出误差调节、内部零动态、层间耦合与参数收敛，并以持续激励和主动阻尼消除残余零空间模态，给出整体渐近稳定性及目标参数轨迹唯一性条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「输出误差收敛不足以确定内部状态、多层网络存在等价输出解流形」及持续激励、零空间模态的处理，可能为 LVR 中迭代 latent 状态更新的稳定性与 latent 轨迹可辨识性提供形式化分析线索，可供核查能否迁移到视觉推理状态。
